title_en: Xinjiang Rural Social Pension Insurance Fund Management Center v. Bank of China, Xinjiang Branch — dispute over certificate of deposit
keywords_en: Civil; Deposit certificate dispute; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Legal person; Financial institution; General Principles of Civil Law; Whether a commercial bank should bear civil liability for failing to confiscate work documents of a dismissed employee; Determination of authenticity of deposit relationship; Reversal of judgment; Continued use of documents by dismissed staff; Forgery of deposit certificates; Good faith; Bank of China Xinjiang Branch deposit certificate dispute
full_text_en:
Xinjiang Rural Social Pension Insurance Fund Management Center  

v.  

Bank of China, Xinjiang Branch  

— Dispute over deposit certificate  

[Ruling Summary]  

In accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, where a commercial bank, after removing an employee from its staff, fails to recover the employee's work identification, allowing the employee to continue to use such identification and to use deposit instruments stamped with the bank's business seal to defraud others of their deposits, thereby causing economic losses to others, the commercial bank shall bear corresponding civil liability.  

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court  

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 34  

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Rural Social Pension Insurance Fund Management Center. Domicile: No. 37, South Xinhua Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.  

Responsible Person: Li Guanzhong, Director of the Center.  

Agent ad litem: Ding Jiang, Lawyer from Yinshi Law Firm.  

Agent ad litem: Zhong Liyang, Lawyer from Yinshi Law Firm.  

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Bank of China, Xinjiang Branch. Domicile: No. 343, South Jiefang Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.  

Responsible Person: Qiu Wanqiang, President of the Branch.  

Agent ad litem: Zheng Siqing, Staff Member of the Branch.  

Agent ad litem: Song Guiping, Lawyer from Xinjiang Shuangyi Law Firm.  

Third Party at First Instance: Urumqi Huaqiao Tourism & Overseas Remittance Service Company. Domicile: No. 81, West Houjie, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.  

Legal Representative: Jiang Jingshu, General Manager of the Company.  

In the dispute over a deposit certificate between the appellant, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Rural Social Pension Insurance Fund Management Center (hereinafter referred to as the Social Security Center), and the respondent, Bank of China, Xinjiang Branch (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiang BOC), and the third party at first instance, Urumqi Huaqiao Tourism & Overseas Remittance Service Company (hereinafter referred to as the Overseas Remittance Company), the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered a civil judgment on April 26, 1999, (1999) Xin Jing Chu Zi No. 10, which had already taken legal effect. That court, by civil ruling (2001) Xin Jing Jian Zi No. 85 on June 5, 2001, decided to retry the case, and on December 12, 2001, rendered a civil judgment (2001) Xin Jing Zai Zi No. 18. The Social Security Center, dissatisfied with that retrial judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court, on the grounds that the original judgment had unclear factual findings and procedural violations, issued a civil ruling on July 31, 2002, (2002) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 100, remanding the case for retrial. The court of first instance rendered a civil judgment on December 5, 2003, (2002) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 48. The Social Security Center, dissatisfied with that civil judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Xu Ruibai, and Acting Judges Wang Xiansen and Yang Yongmei to hear the case. The Clerk was Kong Ling. The trial of this case has now been concluded.  

The court of first instance, upon retrial, found the following facts:  

On April 3, 1998, Zhang Chaojun received a transfer check numbered 07537401 from the Social Security Center. Zhang Chaojun signed on the stub of that transfer check and issued a receipt. The receipt stated: "Received deposit of 8,170,200 yuan from the Social Security Office of the Civil Affairs Department." On the same day, the Social Security Center issued a receipt numbered 9503526 to Zhang Chaojun. The receipt stated: "Paying unit: Tianshan District Office of the City Sub-branch of Bank of China; Subject matter: Interest income; Amount: 829,800 yuan." On the same day, Zhang Chaojun gave the Social Security Center a Bank of China deposit slip. The deposit slip stated: "Payer: Social Security Center; Payee: This unit; Amount: 9,000,000 yuan." On April 13, 1998, Zhang Chaojun gave the Social Security Center a certificate of confirmation for opening a fixed deposit account. The certificate stated: "Civil Affairs Department Social Security Office: Your unit has opened a fixed deposit (lump sum deposit and withdrawal) account at our bank; Amount: 9,000,000 yuan; Term: One year; Interest rate: 5.22%; Teller: Li Ming; Reviewer: Wang Hong." On April 3, 1998, the Overseas Remittance Company issued a certificate to the Social Security Center stating: "Received RMB 9,000,000 in cash transferred by Comrade Zhang Chaojun of the Tianshan Office of Bank of China on behalf of the Social Security Center, after deducting interest of 829,800 yuan; Our unit shall repay the full amount by October 13, 1998, and will endeavor to do so earlier."  

On February 9, 1999, the Second Civil Division of the court of first instance commissioned the Technical Office of that court to conduct a handwriting examination, resulting in the Xin Gao Fa Ji Jian Zi (99) No. 10 Opinion on Handwriting Examination. The conclusion was: The seal impression of "Business Seal of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Bank of China, Urumqi City" on the certificate of confirmation matched certain characteristics of the business seal of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Bank of China, Urumqi City; the handwriting on the certificate of confirmation was written by Zhang Chaojun; the "Bill Exchange" seal impression on the Bank of China deposit slip dated April 3, 1998, was not made by the same seal as that provided by the Tianshan District Office of Bank of China. On September 18, 2000, the People's Procuratorate of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region commissioned the Ministry of Public Security to conduct a physical evidence examination, resulting in the (2000) Gong Wu Zheng Jian Zi No. 88 Opinion on Physical Evidence Examination. The conclusion was: There was a tendency that the Uighur script seal impression of "Business Seal of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Bank of China, Urumqi City" on the examined material and the same content on the sample were made by the same seal. During the original trial of this case, the presiding judge consulted the original examiners as to whether the findings of "partial match of characteristics" and "tendency to be made by the same seal" could constitute a conclusive identification. The original examiners stated: It would not be sufficient to conclude that the seal was the same based only on a partial match of characteristics; the visible parts were the same, but the invisible parts could not be confirmed; the opinion of tendency was mainly for investigative reference and could not serve as evidence.  

The criminal附带 civil judgment rendered by the court of first instance on September 17, 2003, (2003) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 279, found the following:  

1. Zhang Chaojun's confession: On March 28, 1998, Jiang Jingshu called me to the Five-Star Building and told me that Chen Zhihua, the Deputy Director of the Social Security Center, was his fellow townsman and was currently in charge. Jiang had already discussed with Chen Zhihua to let Jiang use RMB 9,000,000 from the Social Security Center. However, it could not be done directly; someone with the identity of a bank employee needed to handle the transfer. At that time, because of my irregularities at work, the bank had suspended me. I left the bank on March 2-3, and later a document was issued to dismiss me. Jiang Jingshu knew all this. Jiang Jingshu called Chen Zhihua from the next room and introduced our identities. He asked me to go to the Civil Affairs Department as the director of the office to solicit deposits, take the money, and directly hand it to Jiang Jingshu. At that time, I told them in front of Chen Zhihua that I had already been transferred and was no longer with the bank. Jiang Jingshu said it didn't matter; the Civil Affairs Department only needed a document for accounting purposes. Chen Zhihua listened but said nothing. On the morning of March 30, Jiang Jingshu called me to the Civil Affairs Department. I went to the Social Security Center as the deputy director of the Tianshan Office of Bank of China to solicit deposits and showed my work ID (Bank of China ID) to the staff there. On April 3, Jiang Jingshu said Chen Zhihua had arranged for me to get the check, and he said they had agreed that the payee line on the check should be left blank. At the Social Security Office, after deducting interest, the staff gave me a check for over 8,000,000 yuan with no payee indicated. I gave them a receipt and said I would bring the deposit slip in a couple of days. Then, as Jiang Jingshu arranged, I went directly to the Overseas Remittance Company and handed the check to Han Kai. Han Kai went alone to the bank to deposit it. Jiang Jingshu told Han Kai to get the deposit slip from the office and to carve another square seal for the transfer receipt based on the seal previously used on the deposit slips. About two hours later, Han Kai returned with a blank deposit slip and the newly carved square seal. As Jiang Jingshu instructed, I filled out the deposit slip, and then Han Kai stamped it with the carved square seal. After this forged deposit slip was delivered to the Social Security Center, 4-5 days later, Jiang Jingshu told me the Center also wanted a certificate of confirmation of deposit. Han Kai, following Jiang Jingshu's instructions, brought a blank certificate of confirmation for unit deposits and gave it to me. I filled it out and told Han Kai that at least two personal seals of the handlers should be on the certificate to make it look authentic. Han Kai then gave me two carved personal seals. The certificate was brought by Han Kai, the contents were filled in by me, and the official seal on it was that of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Bank of China. The official seal was genuine; I took it to the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch to have it stamped. The two personal seals on the certificate were carved by Han Kai. On April 6, after the funds were credited, Jiang Jingshu told me to deliver this forged deposit slip to the Social Security Center.  

2. Witness Ruan Huxin confirmed that the personal seals of Wang Hong and Li Ming on the deposit confirmation certificate were not those of the bank's employees; witness Zhang Jianxin confirmed that the office had no employees named Wang Hong or Li Ming.  

3. Document (1998) No. 13 issued by the Urumqi City Sub-Branch of Bank of China (hereinafter Urumqi BOC) confirmed that Zhang Chaojun had been dismissed from public employment on March 27, 1998. The meeting minutes of Urumqi BOC recorded: Dismissal of Zhang Chaojun from public employment; deduction of three months' post allowance from the director of the Tianshan Office; deduction of six months' post allowance from the deputy director of the Tianshan Office. The content of the minutes was the same as that of Document No. 13.  

4. The report submitted by the Social Security Center to the authorities confirmed: In late March 1998, the suspect Zhang Chaojun, claiming to be the deputy director of the Tianshan Office of Urumqi BOC, came to the Social Security Center to solicit deposits and stated that if the funds were deposited in their bank, a higher interest rate could be offered. On April 3, 1998, Zhang Chaojun took the check, deducted the high-interest portion, and the actual check amount was 8,170,200 yuan. On April 6, a deposit slip was delivered, and on April 13, a certificate of confirmation for fixed deposit (lump sum deposit and withdrawal) issued by the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Bank of China, Urumqi City, was delivered.  

5. In early July of the same year, when the Social Security Center inquired about the deposit, Bank of China informed them that the deposit had not been placed with the bank but had been directly filled in with the name of the Overseas Remittance Company and the check handed to Jiang Jingshu, resulting in the Social Security Center being defrauded of RMB 9,000,000.  

In that criminal附带 civil judgment, the court of first instance determined: Zhang Chaojun, with the intent of illegal possession, used forged financial instruments to defraud the Social Security Center of 8,170,200 yuan, and his conduct constituted the crime of financial instrument fraud.  

On January 11, 1999, the Social Security Center filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, seeking a judgment ordering Xinjiang BOC to pay the principal of the deposit, RMB 9,000,000, and interest, and ordering the Overseas Remittance Company to bear joint and several liability.  

The court of first instance, upon retrial, held: There was no genuine deposit relationship between the Social Security Center and Xinjiang BOC. Based on the examination results, the certificate of confirmation and the deposit slip held by the Social Security Center were both forged; from the flow of funds, the transfer check for 8,170,200 yuan did not enter Xinjiang BOC's account but directly entered the account of the Overseas Remittance Company. On the same day, the Overseas Remittance Company issued a receipt to the Social Security Center acknowledging receipt of the funds. Zhang Chaojun was originally an employee of Xinjiang BOC but was dismissed on March 27, 1998, due to his irregular conduct. Knowing that he had been dismissed, Zhang Chaojun still solicited deposits in the name of a Xinjiang BOC employee and forged the deposit slip and certificate of confirmation. His conduct was determined by the court of first instance in the criminal附带 civil judgment (2003) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 279 to constitute the crime of financial instrument fraud, and Zhang Chaojun was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment. The consequences of Zhang Chaojun's conduct should be borne by himself. Item 4 of Subparagraph 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Trial of Deposit Certificate Dispute Cases provides: In the trial of a deposit certificate dispute case, if sufficient evidence proves that the deposit certificate, deposit slip, statement of account, deposit contract, or other instruments are forged or altered, the people's court shall, upon ascertaining the facts, confirm that the above instruments are invalid and may dismiss the plaintiff's claim based on such instruments. The Social Security Center's claim against Xinjiang BOC lacked legal basis and should not be supported. The Overseas Remittance Company, having acknowledged in the original first instance trial having received 8,170,200 yuan from the Social Security Center, was a third party with a direct interest in this case. The Overseas Remittance Company's possession and use of the funds lacked legal basis and should bear civil liability for returning those funds.  

Pursuant to Article 108 and Paragraph 1 of Article 184 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment:  

Sustain the civil judgment (1999) Xin Jing Chu Zi No. 10 of that court, i.e.:  

1. The Overseas Remittance Company shall return 8,170,200 yuan and interest to the Social Security Center (interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period);  

2. Dismiss the Social Security Center's claim against Xinjiang BOC.  

Court costs for the first instance: 56,576 yuan for case acceptance, 300 yuan for examination fees, 650 yuan for announcement fees, 100 yuan for evidence preservation fees, and 30,040 yuan for property preservation fees, totaling 87,666 yuan, to be borne by the Overseas Remittance Company.  

The Social Security Center, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: The court of first instance's finding that the deposit slip and certificate of confirmation were forged was inconsistent with the facts. The Social Security Center exercised due care in concluding and performing the deposit contract with Xinjiang BOC. During the contract process, the Center sent staff to Xinjiang BOC to verify Zhang Chaojun's identity. When Zhang Chaojun came to the Social Security Center to handle the deposit contract business on behalf of the bank, he held a bank work ID. The business seal of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Urumqi BOC on the certificate of confirmation was genuine. When Zhang Chaojun deposited the 8,170,200 yuan delivered by the Social Security Center into the Overseas Remittance Company, he was a bank employee, and his conduct was an act in the course of employment. Since Zhang Chaojun was the deputy director of the Tianshan Office of Urumqi BOC, the Social Security Center's delivery of the 8,170,200 yuan transfer check to Zhang Chaojun should be deemed as delivery of the check to Xinjiang BOC. As for Zhang Chaojun's subsequent transfer of the funds to the Overseas Remittance Company, that conduct was unrelated to the Social Security Center. The court of first instance erroneously found that the Overseas Remittance Company had issued a receipt to the Social Security Center on the same day acknowledging receipt of the funds. The court of first instance's finding that Xinjiang BOC dismissed Zhang Chaojun on March 27, 1998, and that Zhang Chaojun, knowing of his dismissal, still solicited deposits in the name of Xinjiang BOC, was without legal basis and violated Article 20 of the Regulations on Rewards and Punishments for Enterprise Employees and Article 2 of the Measures for Punishment of Financial Violations. Zhang Chaojun was a bank management official. According to relevant State Council regulations, the dismissal of a bank management official requires the announcement of the dismissal decision at the employing unit, public notice, filing with the local People's Bank of China, and written notification to the individual. Because Xinjiang BOC failed to perform its statutory obligations, Zhang Chaojun was able to have the official seal stamped on the certificate of confirmation at the Heilongjiang Sub-Branch of the Tianshan Office of Urumqi BOC without hindrance. Therefore, Zhang Chaojun's status should still be considered as a bank management official of Xinjiang BOC. Xinjiang BOC had two dismissal decisions with different document numbers: Wu Zhong Yin Zi (1998) No. 6 and Wu Zhong Yin Zi (1998) No. 13. These two documents were not printed at the same time, and the subject heading was "suspension for investigation," yet the content had somehow become a dismissal decision. The criminal附带 civil judgment (2003) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 279 of the court of first instance had numerous issues in procedure, factual findings, and conviction, but the correctly found facts in that judgment included: Zhang Chaojun, while handling the deposit contract with the Social Security Center on behalf of Xinjiang BOC, was still receiving wages from the bank; the official seal of the Heilongjiang Road Sub-Branch of Urumqi BOC on the certificate of confirmation was genuine; Zhang Chaojun held a bank work ID when he went to the Social Security Center to solicit deposits; the dismissal decision was not served on Zhang Chaojun, nor was it announced at his unit or made public; the funds in question entered the Overseas Remittance Company's account. This case is a deposit contract dispute, not a general deposit certificate dispute. Even if Zhang Chaojun's conduct constituted a crime, because the loss of 8,170,200 yuan in farmers' pension funds was directly causally linked to Xinjiang BOC's fault, Xinjiang BOC should bear full civil liability for compensation. That is, whether from a contractual or a tort perspective, Xinjiang BOC should bear civil liability. Therefore, the Social Security Center requested the reversal of the original judgment and a judgment ordering Xinjiang BOC to pay the principal of the deposit, 8,170,200 yuan, and interest to the Social Security Center, with the Overseas Remittance Company bearing joint and several liability for repayment.  

The respondent, Xinjiang BOC, did not submit a written statement of defense. At the second instance cross-examination, it stated: The court of first instance's factual findings were clear and the application of law was correct; therefore, it requested the dismissal of the appeal and the affirmation of the original judgment.  

The third party at first instance, the Overseas Remittance Company, made no statement.  

In addition to essentially affirming the facts found in the first instance, this Court supplemented the following findings:  

The criminal附带 civil judgment (2003) Xin Xing Zhong Zi No. 279 of the court of first instance, rendered on September 17, 2003, based on the confessions of Jiang Jingshu (former general manager of the Overseas Remittance Company), Han Kai, and Zhang Chaojun (former deputy director of the Tianshan Office of Urumqi BOC), as well as other evidence, determined the basic facts of this case as follows: In March 1998, Jiang Jingshu learned that the Social Security Center had RMB 9,000,000 in funds. He contacted Chen Zhihua, Deputy Director of the Finance Division of the Social Security Center, to discuss the use of these funds. Because other leaders of the Social Security Center and the responsible leaders of the Civil Affairs Department insisted that the funds be deposited in a bank, Jiang Jingshu approached Zhang Chaojun (who had applied to resign on March 20, 1998, and was dismissed by the bank on March 27, 1998), asking him to present himself as a bank employee and go to the Social Security Center to solicit the deposit. Zhang Chaojun then went to the Social Security Center, claiming that the bank offered an interest rate of 9.22%, four percentage points higher than the bank's standard rate, and solicited the deposit. After consideration, the Social Security Center agreed to deposit RMB 9,000,000 in the Tianshan Office. On April 3, 1998, following Zhang Chaojun's instructions, the Social Security Center deducted 829,800 yuan in interest and delivered a transfer check for 8,170,200 yuan with no payee filled in to Zhang Chaojun. Following Jiang Jingshu's instructions, Zhang Chaojun handed the transfer check to the defendant Han Kai. At Jiang Jingshu's direction, Han Kai immediately opened an account in the name of the Overseas Remittance Company at the Urumqi Huanyu Credit Union and deposited the 8,170,200 yuan into that account. Thereafter, Jiang Jingshu, together with Zhang Chaojun and Han Kai, forged a Bank of China deposit slip for RMB 9,000,000 and a certificate of confirmation for fixed deposit. Zhang Chaojun gave these forged documents to the Social Security Center, thereby taking possession of the 8,170,200 yuan. After the case was discovered, cash of RMB 700,000 and a Hainan Mazda sedan were recovered from Han Kai. The dismissal decision of Urumqi BOC regarding Zhang Chaojun was not served on Zhang Chaojun personally, nor was it publicly announced. Based on these facts, the criminal附带 civil judgment of the court of first instance determined that the conduct of Jiang Jingshu, Zhang Chaojun, and Han Kai constituted the crime of financial instrument fraud. It sentenced Jiang Jingshu to life imprisonment, Zhang Chaojun to 15 years' imprisonment, and Han Kai to 6 years' imprisonment, and ordered the recovery of the 700,000 yuan and the Hainan Mazda sedan, which were to be returned to the Social Security Center.

Opinion of the Court: This case involves the intersection of civil disputes and criminal offenses. When this Court remanded the case for retrial, the court of first instance had not yet rendered a criminal judgment. During the retrial, the court of first instance ascertained the relevant facts of this case and has rendered a criminal附带民事 judgment. According to the basic facts found in that judgment, Jiang Jingshu, in collusion with Zhang Chaojun and Han Kai, obtained funds from the Social Security Center by forging payment slips and certificates of fixed-term deposits, and their conduct constituted the crime of financial instrument fraud. The court of first instance, while sentencing the aforementioned Zhang Chaojun and others to life imprisonment or fixed-term imprisonment, also ordered that the recovered illicit funds of RMB 700,000 and a Hainan Mazda sedan be returned to the Social Security Center. In handling the civil dispute in this case, consideration should be given to the basic facts found in the criminal judgment. The finding in the original judgment that no genuine deposit relationship existed between the Social Security Center and Xinjiang BOC was not improper. However, the absence of a genuine deposit relationship between the Social Security Center and Xinjiang BOC only indicates that no contractual relationship existed between the parties and that Xinjiang BOC was not liable for contractual liability; this alone does not necessarily lead to the conclusion that Xinjiang BOC should bear no civil liability whatsoever in this case.

Based on the criminal conduct of Jiang Jingshu, Zhang Chaojun, and Han Kai, Qiaohui Company took possession of the amount of RMB 8,170,200 in this case without lawful basis and should return that amount to the Social Security Center. The original judgment ordering Qiaohui Company to return RMB 8,170,200 and interest to the Social Security Center was not improper, and Qiaohui Company did not appeal; therefore, that part of the judgment should be upheld. As to whether Xinjiang BOC should bear civil liability in this case, this concerns the issue of whether Xinjiang BOC was at fault for the success of the fraud by Zhang Chaojun and others. Where there is fault, civil liability should be borne; this is the basic connotation of the principle of fault liability in civil law. From the basic facts of this case, before the conduct in question occurred, although Zhang Chaojun was dismissed by Urumqi BOC on March 27, 1998, Xinjiang BOC did not confiscate Zhang Chaojun's work identification card, with the result that Zhang Chaojun, still using the capacity of Deputy Director of the Tianshan Office of Urumqi BOC and holding the bank's work identification card, solicited deposits from the Social Security Center; in particular, Zhang Chaojun delivered to the Social Security Center a certificate of fixed-term deposit stamped with the business seal of the Heilongjiang Sub-branch of Urumqi BOC. Regarding the authenticity of the official seal affixed on that certificate, the appraisal conclusions made upon the commission of the technical office of the court of first instance and the appraisal conclusions made upon the commission of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region People's Procuratorate to the Material Evidence Identification Center of the Ministry of Public Security were substantially consistent. The above two appraisal conclusions were also substantially consistent with the confessions of Zhang Chaojun. Therefore, it should be determined that the business seal of the Heilongjiang Sub-branch of Urumqi BOC affixed on the certificate of fixed-term deposit was genuine. Since Zhang Chaojun, after being dismissed from public office by Urumqi BOC, was still able to use a certificate of fixed-term deposit bearing the unit's official seal, this indicates that Urumqi BOC had fault in its management, and this fault was an important reason for the success of the fraud by Zhang Chaojun and others. Therefore, Xinjiang BOC should bear corresponding civil liability for its fault. The Social Security Center did not go to the bank counter to complete the deposit procedures and readily trusted the actions of Zhang Chaojun and others, which also indicates that it was at fault and should bear corresponding civil liability on its own.

In summary, the findings of fact by the court of first instance were basically clear. However, in the application of law, apart from ordering Qiaohui Company to return RMB 8,170,200 and interest to the Social Security Center, the court of first instance erred in dismissing the Social Security Center's claim against Xinjiang BOC, and this Court should correct that error. The Social Security Center's ground of appeal that Xinjiang BOC should bear civil liability in this case is well-founded and should be supported by this Court. Pursuant to Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby rules as follows:

1. Affirm Item 1 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2002) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 48 rendered by the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, that is, Urumqi Huaqiao Overseas Chinese Travel and Remittance Service Company shall return RMB 8,170,200 and interest calculated in segments according to the同期 loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China to the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Rural Social Pension Insurance Fund Management Center;

2. Reverse Item 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2002) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 48 rendered by the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region;

3. Bank of China Xinjiang Branch shall bear compensatory liability for the amount stated in Item 1 of the judgment above within the scope of 50% of the principal and interest that Urumqi Huaqiao Overseas Chinese Travel and Remittance Service Company is unable to repay.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 56,576, appraisal fee of RMB 300, announcement fee of RMB 650, evidence preservation fee of RMB 100, and property preservation fee of RMB 30,040, totaling RMB 87,666, shall be borne as per the original judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 56,576 shall be borne by the Social Security Center in the amount of RMB 28,288 and by Xinjiang BOC in the amount of RMB 28,288.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Xu Ruibai

Acting Judge: Wang Xiansen

Acting Judge: Yang Yongmei

April 28, 2004

Clerk: Kong Ling

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Xu Ruibai, Senior Judge: Born in 1963, Bachelor of Laws, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 1994.
